headline: Local Tea Stall Owner Confirms He Has 'Political Ambitions' After Correctly Predicting Rain Twice in One Week
body:
Ramesh Gupta, who operates a modest tea kiosk near the state secretariat, officially declared his entry into the political arena this morning after an uncanny two-week streak of accurately predicting light showers. Emboldened by his growing reputation as a meteorological oracle, Gupta announced that his 'Chai-And-Change' platform will prioritize umbrella subsidies and mandatory ginger-to-tea ratios for the upcoming municipal elections.

"It’s time to stop pretending that brewing a perfect cup of adrak-chai is my only contribution to society," Gupta stated while deftly straining a fresh batch for a line of curious commuters. "People ask if I have an agenda beyond serving hot beverages. Of course I do. I want to reform the local gutter system and perhaps legislate a maximum wait time for morning buses. Just because I handle kettles doesn't mean I don't harbor deep, structural plans for the ward."

Local residents, who previously visited the stall only for the biscuits, seem divided on the sudden shift. "He told me it would drizzle on Tuesday, and he was right—I didn't bring my raincoat and I was soaked," noted regular patron Sunil Mehta. "If he can manage the clouds, surely he can manage the local sewage budget. It’s not like he’s a saint, he clearly wants the corner office, but at least he knows how to keep the chai strong."
caption: From serving cutting chai to cutting budget deficits—the political landscape just got a little more caffeinated. ☕️🗳️ #LocalPolitics #ChaiPolitics #ElectionSeason (satire)
igHook: Would you vote for your local tea stall owner if they promised better weather forecasting?
